candidates.note: O parâmetro livre 'param' é atribuído via params.get(param), que pode retornar None ou qualquer valor não bool. Não há guarda que impeça que 'param' seja None ou tipo diferente de bool antes do assert, portanto o assert pode falhar e gerar AssertionError alcançável.

The parameter 'ind' is derived by taking the indices from np.searchsorted and slicing [1:-1], which can result in ind being empty or having elements potentially out of range when used for indexing next. Since no guard validates if ind is not empty and all indices are within valid range, accessing y0[ind] or y1[ind - 1] or x[ind] can cause out-of-bounds indexing if ind contains elements 0 or greater than len(x) - 1.

In the denominator, (x[ind] - x[ind - 1]) can be zero if x[ind] == x[ind - 1], causing a division by zero. Although x is strictly increasing, no guard explicitly ensures that ind values are valid indices and that denominator differences are strictly positive. Because ind is derived dynamically and can potentially select invalid indices or positions leading to zero denominator (for example, repeated x values or incorrect ind from searchsorted), a ZeroDivisionError is possible.

num_substrings is assigned len(possible_substrings_splits[i]) which can be zero if possible_substrings_splits[i] is an empty list; the code divides by num_substrings without checking if it is zero, causing a potential ZeroDivisionError.
Same as above; division by num_substrings without checking if num_substrings is zero can cause ZeroDivisionError if possible_substrings_splits[i] is empty.

Indexing possible_substrings_splits[i][j] assumes it is aligned with possible_parsed_splits[i], but there's no guard to ensure both have same length or j is valid index for possible_substrings_splits[i]. This can raise IndexError if lengths differ.

Os parâmetros range_end e range_begin são usados para calcular o denominador da operação de módulo. Eles são controlados externamente e não possuem guarda para garantir que range_end seja maior que range_begin, o que pode tornar a expressão (range_end - range_begin + 1) zero ou negativa, causando divisão por zero na operação modulo.

The parameter chunk_size controls wdw_size, which derives step_size as wdw_size - 1. If chunk_size is 1, step_size is zero, leading to a division by zero in math.ceil((h_src - wdw_size) / step_size) + 1 in the for loop range, causing a runtime error.

Indices i_h_src_056 and i_w_src_056 are computed from i_h_y+i_h_x and i_w_y+i_w_x, which are derived from ranges without explicit bounds checks. These indices may be out of bounds if h_tile_size_src or w_src is 0 or 1, or near the edges causing indices exceeding dims. Thus indexing in_tile may cause IndexError if indices exceed input shape limits.

Indices i_h_src_006 and i_w_src_006 involve computation i_h_y + (-1 * i_h_x + 1) and i_w_y + (-1 * i_w_x +1), creating possible negative indices or indices too large. Without guard checking ranges, these indices might access out-of-bounds positions causing IndexError.
Similar to other index computations, i_h_src_018_h = i_h_y + (-1 * i_h_x + 1) and i_w_src_018_h = i_w_y + i_w_x can go out of bounds without guards. Hence out-of-bounds indexing is possible.
Computed indices i_h_src_018_w and i_w_src_018_w involve expressions that may produce out-of-range indices without explicit guards preventing access out of src_arr bounds, risking IndexError.

Here i_w_src is (w_src - 1) * i_w, which is either 0 or w_src-1, but i_h_src_075 can be at edge indices. Without checks, accessing in_tile might cause IndexError if shape dimensions are small or zero.
Similar to above, indexing in_tile without bounds validation may cause IndexError due to potentially negative or out-of-range indices from i_h_src_025.

Indices i_h_src = (h_tile_size_src - 1) * i_h and i_w_src = (w_src - 1) * i_w involve multiplication by values from i_h and i_w indices (0 or 1). Without range checks, these can result in out-of-bounds if h_tile_size_src or w_src are invalid or dimensions zero, causing IndexError.

The parameter 'clocs' is controlled externally and assumed to be index level names or integers. The function calls index._get_level_number(i) on each element of clocs without explicit validation. If 'clocs' contains values that are not valid level names or indexes, _get_level_number(i) can raise an exception (e.g., KeyError). There is no guard to prevent invalid level names or indices in clocs, so this can cause failure.

The dummy Index or MultiIndex constructed has a last level named '__placeholder__'. The unstack is performed on this placeholder level, assumed to exist. If the dummy_index does not have '__placeholder__' level due to empty or small input, unstack throws exception. There is no explicit guard ensuring dummy_index contains the level '__placeholder__' before unstack. Since dummy_index is built dynamically and external data may affect levels, this can cause a failure.

The method rec.take is called with unstcols.codes[-1] as argument. If unstcols.codes[-1] contains indices that are out of bounds for rec, or rec is not compatible, this can raise an exception. There is no explicit guard to ensure codes indices are valid for rec.take. As these are derived from data and dynamic MultiIndex manipulations, invalid indexing can occur causing failure.
